newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia steel firm equity open to other buyers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia steel firm equity open to other buyers.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has said the government is willing to sell part of its equity in troubled national steel firm Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd to any company willing to participate in the privatisation.

He said some of the 49 percent stake held by the federal government and the Terengganu state government in Perwaja could be given to the interested party, the national Bernama news agency reported on Monday.

"Lion Group can still take part if it wants to. We are open," Mahathir told reporters earlier on Monday. Lion Group was part of the original rescue plan for the loss-making steel firm, but later opted out.

The majority stake of 51 percent is held by Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd, the bumiputra (ethnic Malay) group heading the turnaround of Perwaja, whose 2.9 billion ringgit ($1.15 billion) in losses will be assumed by the government.
"The government will take over the debts and losses," Mahathir told reporters.
"We will have to find sources of funds to pay off the debts. Of course, the losses may have to be written off. The debts, we will have to pay. There is no way we can avoid paying debts," he added.
The government holds 1.2 billion ringgit of Perwaja debt, with 2.5 billion ringgit held by local banks. Another 3.1 billion ringgit is held by foreign financial institutions.
